ai.description: This 20–25 mm frog is brown with a dark interorbital bar and a pale snout. It features granular skin, a white belly, and distinct reddish-brown webbing between its toes. IUCN: Endangered.
ai.identificationRemarks: The most reliable diagnostic feature of *Raorchestes munnarensis* is the presence of distinct, prominent glandular folds on its dorsum, which are absent in similar species.
ai.habitat: The Munnar bush frog inhabits high-altitude shola forests and adjacent tea plantations in the Western Ghats, typically at elevations above 1,500 meters.
ai.behavior: The Munnar bush frog is primarily nocturnal, emerging at night to forage for small insects among the foliage of its high-altitude habitat in the Western Ghats.
ai.reproductionNotes: *Raorchestes munnarensis* undergoes direct development, bypassing the tadpole stage. It breeds during the monsoon, laying small clutches of eggs in vegetation.
ai.distributionRemarks: The Munnar bush frog is endemic to the high-altitude shola forests of the Munnar region in Kerala, Western Ghats, typically occurring at elevations above 1,500 meters.
ai.callDescription: The Munnar Bush Frog emits a series of high-pitched, insect-like "tink" notes, typically heard from vegetation within its high-altitude shola forest habitat.
